articles.headline: Global power ranking: The top 20 soccer teams in the world, ranked!
articles.description: If we look beyond the Premier League and beyond those who qualified for the Champions League, which are the best teams in the world?
articles.headlineJa: 世界のパワーランキング：世界トップ20サッカーチームをランク付け！
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグやチャンピオンズリーグ出場チームの枠を超えて、世界最強のチームはどこなのか？
articles.body:
Which is the best soccer team in the world?

It might seem easy to answer, and maybe it is. Paris Saint-Germain have won the Champions League two seasons in a row, and they just beat Manchester City and Barcelona, 4-2 in consecutive league-phase matches.

But what about after PSG? Is it Arsenal or Bayern Munich, who just tied each other? Is it Barcelona, who just lost back-to-back games to PSG and Real Madrid? Is it Real Madrid, who are in third place in their league? Is it Manchester City who, uh ... [frantically waves arms toward the 114 charges they were just found guilty of].

And beyond that top tier, are some midtable Premier League clubs better than Champions League qualifiers in Germany? How many English teams would be the favorites to win Serie A? How many Serie A teams would be the second-best team in Germany? And what about, um, Ligue 1?

We will try to address those questions now, and for the rest of the season, with these power rankings of the top 20 teams in the world.

Because any kind of cross-league analytical model would require various, increasingly subjective decisions from me, these instead will be my subjective rankings. In other words, who do I think would win more often if these teams played 100 games on a neutral field?

Along with the rankings below, each team is accompanied by a number of stats from their domestic league: how many points they've won, their non-penalty adjusted goal differential (a blend of 70% expected goals and 30% goals), and the average Opta power rating of their league opponents thus far (not adjusted for home and away).

Now, on to the top 20 list!

1. Paris Saint-Germain

- Points (place): 17, 1st

- Adjusted goal differential (rank): 0.93, 1st

- Strength of opponent (rank): 86.3, T-4th

I'm taking a "first place until proven otherwise" approach with PSG after the past two seasons. Over their back-to-back Champions League run, they've been brought to penalties twice -- one in each year -- by the champions of the best league in the world, Liverpool and then Arsenal, and both of those teams required borderline-absurd, conservative, defensive approaches to get there.

The big question from here: How will they cope with losing Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for the season?

2. Bayern Munich

- Points (place): 17, 1st

- Adjusted goal differential (rank): 2.42, 1st

- Strength of opponent (rank): 86.0, 15th

You could look at their home draw with Arsenal as a negative, given they were -- you know -- at home. But they probably should've won, despite Michael Olise and Joshua Kimmich missing the match and Luis Díaz featuring for just a handful of minutes at the end.

There's a gap, in my mind, between No. 1 and No. 2 in these rankings, but the gulf between No. 2 and No. 3 is the size of "Bukayo Saka being expected to miss a month-plus with a hamstring injury."

3. Arsenal

- Points (place): 21, 2nd

- Adjusted goal differential (rank): 0.94, 2nd

- Strength of opponent (rank): 91.9, 17th

articles.headline: Man United Munich air disaster memorial vandalised
articles.description: A memorial for the 1958 Munich air disaster has been vandalised.
articles.headlineJa: マン・ユナイテッド、ミュンヘン航空機事故の慰霊碑が損壊される
articles.descriptionJa: 1958年のミュンヘン航空機事故の慰霊碑が、損壊された。
articles.body:
A memorial for the 1958 Munich air disaster has been vandalised.

Twenty-three people -- including eight Manchester United players and three staff -- were killed when their plane crashed on a Munich runway in February 1958.

A commemorative glass box, which also houses Man United memorabilia, was set up in "Manchesterplatz" in Munich to mark the tragedy.

Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF) has confirmed the display case was broken into and various items were stolen. 

The foundation said the club offered to pay for repairs, but MMMF had already done so.

"The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation is deeply saddened by this act of vandalism and theft," MMMF chair Ifty Ahmed said.

"Manchesterplatz is a place of enormous significance to the families of the 23 people who lost their lives as a result of the Munich Air Disaster, and to Manchester United supporters across the world.

"We are particularly grateful to our friends in Munich, especially the Red Docs, for their continued care and dedication to this very special place, and for acting so swiftly to repair the damage.

"Those responsible may have damaged a display case and stolen treasured items, but they cannot steal our memories, diminish our friendship or destroy the legacy of those we remember.

"Their memory will endure, and the bond between Manchester and Munich will remain unbreakable."

articles.headline: Packers' Josh Jacobs: TD celebration was ode to gospel song, not mocking arrest
articles.description: The Packers' Josh Jacobs said he was surprised his first-half TD celebration was perceived by some as mocking his May arrest, saying it was an ode to a gospel song.
articles.headlineJa: パッカーズのジョシュ・ジェイコブス：TDセレブレーションはゴスペルへのオマージュであり、逮捕を揶揄したものではない
articles.descriptionJa: パッカーズのジョシュ・ジェイコブスは、前半のTDセレブレーションが5月の逮捕を揶揄していると一部に受け取られたことに驚きを示し、あれはゴスペルソングへのオマージュだったと語った。
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- When Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs scored the first of his two touchdowns in Thursday night's 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers, the broadcast cameras showed him celebrating in the end zone with his hands behind his back.

The video quickly went viral, considering Jacobs had been arrested earlier this year and was charged with misdemeanor battery and destruction of property following an incident with a woman at his Green Bay area home.

After the game, Jacobs was not happy that people connected the arrest with his celebration, which he said was an ode to a gospel song called "Break Every Chain."

"They didn't even get the whole celebration," Jacobs said, adding, "It was f---ing one second that they just showed me."

Jacobs, who returned last week after spending the first six games of the season on the commissioner exempt list, said he and receiver Savion Williams came up with two celebrations upon his return.

"Basically, last week, we said the first celebration, when I score, I was going to thank God -- that's what I did last week," Jacobs said. "The second one was going to be 'Break Every Chain.' It's a gospel song. That was going to be the next celebration. It's just a correlation, but like I said, the media [is] going to run with it. They're going to make it something that it wasn't, but it is what it is."

Jacobs said several of his teammates made the same gesture during the touchdown celebration.

"I didn't think it was going to be a thing that can be perceived a certain type of way," Jacobs said. "But it's 2026, and it is what it is."

Jacobs pleaded no contest to the charges in September. He was convicted of battery and was given a deferred judgment agreement on the destruction of property charge. The NFL took him off the commissioner exempt list in Week 7, but the league has not closed its investigation into violations of the personal conduct policy.

Jacobs made his season debut Sunday against the Lions, but Thursday's game was his first at Lambeau Field this season. He said the reception from the fans was positive.

"It was good, man," he said. "I think it was good. I think it was good for the team. It was good to be out there, Thursday night, electric, stadium packed. As an offense, we had our little lull moments, but the defense held it down in this game."

Jacobs rushed for just 39 yards on 21 carries (a 1.9-yard average) against the league's worst rushing defense. His touchdown was a 1-yard run. He also caught six passes for 13 yards, including a 4-yard touchdown in the third quarter.

articles.headline: Panthers' Bryce Young says injured knee 'fine' after taking 6 sacks vs. Packers
articles.description: Panthers quarterback Bryce Young was pressured on nearly half his dropbacks and was sacked six times, but said his injured knee was "fine" after a 27-19 loss to the Packers.
articles.headlineJa: パンサーズのブライス・ヤング、パッカーズ戦で6回のサックを受けるも、負傷した膝は「大丈夫」と語る
articles.descriptionJa: パンサーズのクォーターバック、ブライス・ヤングは、プレーのほぼ半分でプレッシャーを受け、6回のサックを浴びたが、パッカーズに27-19で敗れた後、負傷した膝は「大丈夫だ」と述べた。
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young couldn't escape the pressure against the Green Bay Packers' pass rush Thursday night at Lambeau Field. He was pressured early and often behind a makeshift offensive line, and with a brace affixed to his left knee, his typical fluidity in the pocket appeared to be somewhat compromised.

Young's left knee, which was injured in a Week 3 road loss to the Cleveland Browns, hadn't held him back in previous weeks, but in the team's 27-19 loss to the Packers, he failed to regularly create and extend plays with his trademark quickness.

And yet, Young -- who was pressured on 48.9% of his dropbacks and threw just one pass of 20 yards or more against the Packers, according to NFL Next Gen Stats -- refused to use his knee as an excuse.

"I'm fine," Young said. "Everyone's dealing with something at this point. It's football. Nothing like that is an excuse. Go out there, play the game -- blessed to be able to do that. That's all that matters."

Young was pressured on 22 pass plays. He was sacked six times and completed just 6 of 16 passes for 46 yards and an interception when under duress.

He was hit nine times.

"I would say that he certainly doesn't look like he's got that quick, make-you-miss-type of deal, but he was able to create some space for himself," coach Dave Canales said. "But the rush got after us, and that's the bottom line. We've got to take care of that first part of it, so we have an element of time to be able to execute the play."

Early-season waiver-wire pickup Corey Bullock filled in for starting left guard Damien Lewis for the second time in four games. But Bullock was eventually replaced after suffering a quad injury in the third quarter. Practice-squad call-up Jake Curhan, a journeyman who played in 13 games (one start) for the Panthers last year, filled in for him.

"It's kind of what I've been doing for the last five years, six years," Curhan said about the spot duty. "You've got to get into that rhythm, into that flow. Unfortunately, it took me one bad play [a sack allowed in the third quarter] to get in it. Otherwise, I felt pretty good. Was a little [frustrated] about that one, but nothing you can do but move on."

According to Next Gen Stats, Young faced more than half of his pressures (13 of 22) from the edge. First-round pick Monroe Freeling, who was starting at right tackle again with Taylor Moton (fibula/ankle) done for the season, struggled to maintain his pass protection throughout the game.

Next Gen Stats flagged Freeling with four total pressures and a sack allowed.

"It's all about opportunities," Freeling said. "You're given opportunities, you've got to capitalize on them. And if you don't, you don't win."

articles.headline: Trail Blazers' Ja Morant exits first game vs. Grizzlies with hamstring injury
articles.description: Ja Morant exited his first game against his former team in the fourth quarter Thursday night because of a left hamstring injury.
articles.headlineJa: トレイルブレイザーズのジャ・モラント、グリズリーズ戦の初戦でハムストリングの負傷により退場
articles.descriptionJa: ジャ・モラントは木曜夜、古巣との初戦において、左ハムストリングの負傷により第4クォーターで退場した。
articles.body:
Portland Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant exited his first game against his former team in the fourth quarter Thursday night because of a left hamstring injury.

Morant had 14 points and three assists in 23 minutes before exiting and being ruled out of the Trail Blazers' 124-103 loss to the Memphis Grizzlies.

Coach Micah Nori said postgame that Morant felt a twinge in his hamstring and that Nori hoped to have more answers Friday.

"I'm hoping that it's nothing major, obviously," Nori said.

Morant, in his first season with Portland after spending the first seven years of his career with Memphis, averaged 16.3 points and 6.3 assists in 26.7 minutes as the Trail Blazers began the season 3-0 before picking up their first loss Thursday.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Sources: New Milan, Inter stadium gets $725M naming rights deal with Generali
articles.description: AC Milan and Inter Milan have agreed a naming rights deal with Italian insurance giant Generali for the new San Siro.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：ミラン、インテルの新スタジアム、ジェネラリと7億2500万ドルのネーミングライツ契約を締結
articles.descriptionJa: ACミランとインテル・ミランは、新しいサン・シーロ・スタジアムのネーミングライツについて、イタリアの保険大手ジェネラリと合意した。
articles.body:
AC Milan and Inter Milan announced that they have agreed a naming rights deal with Italian insurance company Generali for their new stadium, which is set to open in 2031.

The clubs said in a news release Thursday that the deal represented "one of the largest stadium naming rights agreements in global sport."

Sources confirmed to ESPN that the deal is worth €650 million ($725 million) over 20 years.

In November 2021, Crypto.com paid a reported $700 million over 20 years -- at the time believed to be the richest naming rights deal in sports history -- to rename the downtown Los Angeles home of the NBA's Lakers, the NHL's Kings and the WNBA's Sparks.

The agreement with Generali was announced at an event in which the renderings for the new 71,500-seat venue, to be named Generali Stadium, were revealed.

The project is being driven by the club's respective owners, AC Milan's RedBird Capital Partners and Inter's Oaktree.

The stadium's architects feature a collaboration between Foster+Partners and MANICA, bringing together Lord Norman Foster and David Manica. The two architects previously collaborated on the design of London's Wembley Stadium.

The project will now go through design and planning phase. Construction is expected to begin in 2028 and the first match targeted for the 2031-32 season, subject to the necessary approvals. The project is also part of a broader urban regeneration plan for the area that will include public spaces, green areas as well as leisure and retail spaces.

According to a joint news release from both clubs, the design is inspired by "the intricate craftsmanship of the Duomo di Milano." Two seating tiers will form a continuous 360-degree bowl.

Originally built in 1926, the San Siro, with its striking spiral staircases wrapped around the outside of the stadium, was renovated for the 1990 World Cup but lacks the facilities offered by other top European football venues.

At either end, the iconic "Curvas" will rise as single, steep walls, drawing fans forward toward the field of play.

Seating inclinations of up to 37 degrees will amplify both atmosphere and visual impact.

According to the release, the intention is to "bring supporters closer than ever before to the moments that matter most."

AC Milan and Inter Milan bought the land for the stadium off the city last November for €197 million ($230 million), paving the way for its demolition and the construction of a new venue. The two Serie A clubs have long shared the use of the historic ground, but see building a joint modern arena as vital to boosting their matchday revenue, which lags behind their European rivals.

Italy is under growing pressure to upgrade the quality of its stadiums, driven by foreign investors backing Serie A clubs and the need for more functional venues for the 2032 European Championship, which it will co-host with Türkiye.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool in contact over Monaco's Camara
articles.description: Liverpool have reached out to representatives of Lamine Camara and will explore a transfer next summer. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Liverpool are keeping tabs on AS Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, while Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford could be heading to Everton on loan.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool have made contact with the representatives of AS Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and have asked to be kept informed of his future, as per The Sun. While a January switch has been ruled out, after a €55 million move to Chelsea fell through over the summer, both clubs will explore a transfer for the 22-year-old Senegal international next year.

- Everton are weighing up a January loan for Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford on a deal similar to that of Manchester City winger Jack Grealish, according to Football Insider. The 28-year-old England international has returned to United's squad following previous loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona, but has yet to register a goal contribution this season and could be looking for a way out.

articles.headline: PSG's Luis Enrique: Vitinha deserved higher Ballon d'Or ranking
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique does not believe star midfielder Vitinha got the recognition he deserved in the Ballon d'Or rankings.
articles.headlineJa: PSGのルイス・エンリケ監督、ヴィティーニャはバロンドールでより高い順位にふさわしかったと主張
articles.descriptionJa: パリ・サンジェルマンのルイス・エンリケ監督は、スターミッドフィルダーのヴィティーニャがバロンドールのランキングで正当な評価を得られたと考えていない。
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique does not believe star midfielder Vitinha got the recognition he deserved in the Ballon d'Or rankings.

The back-to-back Champions League winners head to rock-bottom Le Havre on Friday evening having moved top of Ligue 1 with last weekend's 2-0 win against Lyon.

PSG return to action fresh from being crowned Men's Club of the Year at the 70th Ballon d'Or ceremony, when 10 of their players were among the 30 nominees for the men's award.

Vitinha was among those and ended up 14th, a year on from finishing third when team-mate Ousmane Dembélé lifted the trophy.

PSG boss Enrique said of the Portugal international: "It's a real pleasure to have a player with such technical and physical ability. His level is incredible.

"We're very pleased to have a player of his calibre, even though he wasn't ranked as highly as he deserves to be in the Ballon d'Or rankings."

Sixth-placed Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was PSG's highest-ranked player at the Ballon d'Or and this week underwent surgery in Qatar on a torn anterior cruciate ligament.

Dembélé finished seventh and is another missing for Friday's game at Le Havre, as are Nuno Mendes and Marquinhos after recording 23rd and 25th place finishes.

PSG said the trio "all continue their rehabilitation" and head coach Enrique said: "We like to have as much control as possible, and the issue of injuries has been a major focus of our work in recent years.

"Some players suffer injuries more frequently than others, so it can sometimes be difficult to control. We aim to refine and optimise the training load to minimise the number of injured players.

"Throughout my coaching career, we've always sought to manage this; there have been tough times and better times, but I'm pleased with what we're trying to achieve.

"However, it's always difficult because injuries are part and parcel of top-flight football."

PSG have the strength in depth to cope, even with a Champions League match at Villarreal and home game against Troyes following the perennial Ligue 1 champions' game at winless Le Havre.

Enrique knows the pressure is on them to stay in their "favourite position" and wants to continue building as they head to the Stade Océane seeking a ninth straight win in all competitions.

articles.headline: Crystal Palace's Ismaïla Sarr set to be sidelined for weeks, Pierre Sage confirms
articles.description: Ismaïla Sarr is likely to remain sidelined with a groin issue until after the international break, Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage has confirmed.
articles.headlineJa: クリスタル・パレスのイスマイラ・サール、数週間の離脱へ。ピエール・サージュが認める
articles.descriptionJa: クリスタル・パレスのピエール・サージュ監督は、イスマイラ・サールが鼠径部の問題により、代表ウィーク明けまで戦線を離脱する可能性が高いことを認めた。
articles.body:
Ismaïla Sarr is likely to remain sidelined with a groin issue until after the international break, Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage has confirmed.

The Senegal international was last season's Conference League top scorer, but has made just five appearances for Palace across all competitions so far.

Palace have lost one of those five games, while they have been beaten in five of the eight matches he has missed, but the under-pressure Sage will have to do without him for at least the next three outings before the November international window.

When asked about when the 28-year-old might be available again, Sage said: "I think after the international break."

The under-pressure Eagles boss secured a big Carabao Cup win at Fulham on Wednesday night, and will now look to turn Palace's Premier League fortunes around at Tottenham before hosting Hoffenheim in the Europa League, then welcoming Liverpool to Selhurst Park before the pause.

Asked if he might prefer to be taking on their subsequent league opponents -- Coventry and Hull -- Sage said: "Every point smells good, and if we take points against Liverpool or Tottenham or against the other team, it's the same for us at the end, because we need, and we will play all the game to take points.

"We are not in a position to choose one game better than another. We do, we did, and we will do the same with the cups and the league too. That's why we made some rotations, because we wanted to win on Wednesday, but we wanted to create the conditions of freshness for Saturday too.

"At the moment that strategy is good, but we have to confirm that and go until the goal we fixed at the beginning of the week."

Sage confirmed Jean-Philippe Mateta was rested against Fulham but will be ready to start against Tottenham.

Jorgen Strand Larsen continues to recover from the ankle issue he sustained in their 2-2 draw with Besiktas last week, and will train with the group on Thursday afternoon.

Sage confirmed Quinten Timber could also potentially feature in the Spurs clash, which should also feature captain Dean Henderson who recovered well on his first start back from injury on Wednesday.

Palace sit one place and point clear of the relegation zone heading into Sunday's trip to north London, and there has been some suggestion that this weekend could be a major test of the front office's faith that Sage remains the right man for the job.
